subject: Medita: third-party evidence — subprocessor list, SBOM, and KMS ownership
messages:
From: Sarah Lang <sarah.lang@medita.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@medita.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Supply chain artifacts request — subprocessor roster, SBOM, KMS ownership

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. Medita's procurement/security team is running a routine third-party risk intake ahead of our platform pilot. We need to validate a handful of artifacts so our InfoSec can complete the assessment:

- Current subprocessor roster (name, primary function, country, whether they have access to customer data or to the runtime infra)
- SBOM for the inference runtime + serving container (package names, versions, hashes) — redacted source is OK but we need deterministic hashes for our scanner
- KMS / key custody summary: who holds encryption keys for customer data (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private), HSM/KMS brand(s), and whether BYOK or re-encryption occurs during migration/backups
- Latest SOC 2 Type II report (or SOC 2 + roadmap to obtain it if Type II not available) and SIG/CAIQ point-of-contact or completion ETA

Can you confirm whether you can provide these items and an expected delivery date? We need the artifacts by COB Thursday (5 business days) to avoid delaying our security approval. If there are items that cannot be shared verbatim, please indicate what redaction/attestation options exist.

Appreciate it,
Sarah
Sarah Lang
Security Programs Manager
Medita Health

Subject: Re: Supply chain artifacts request — subprocessor roster, SBOM, KMS ownership

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. We can provide the items you requested; a couple quick clarifications so we scope correctly:

- Do you require signed attestations for the subprocessor roster or will a timestamped CSV with contact points and roles be sufficient?
- For the SBOM, is a JSON manifest (package name/version/hash) plus a short README acceptable, or do you need container image manifests (we can provide both if required)?
- On KMS: are you looking for a high-level custody statement or an operational runbook (e.g., key rotation, backup re-encryption steps)?

We will assemble the artifacts and propose to share a redacted SBOM and the SOC 2 PDF via a secure shared drive link. Marcus — can you pull the latest subprocessor export and draft the KMS summary?

I can target delivery by end-of-day Thu (Nov 18). If you prefer a quick 20-minute call to walk through the artifacts, happy to schedule.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Supply chain artifacts request — subprocessor roster, SBOM, KMS ownership

Vanessa — adding details below and attaching draft artifacts for review. Notes:

1) Subprocessor roster (attached: redwood_subprocessors_20261116.csv) — fields: provider_name, service_area, country, data_access (none/runtime/customer_data), contact, last_review_date. This list includes short-lived infra contractors (ephemeral CI/CD runners) in a single consolidated line item (we avoid exposing transient vendor hostnames). If Medita needs the short-lived provider names included verbatim we can propose a redacted per-tenant attestation.

2) SBOM (attached: sbom-inference-runtime-202611.json) — this is a generated manifest of packages and hashes for the inference runtime and the launcher container. It includes deterministic hashes for all third-party binaries. We cannot share internal build scripts or private source code, but the manifest should satisfy automated scanners.

3) KMS / key custody (attached: kms-ownership-summary-202611.docx) — summary: for Hosted API customers, Redwood manages envelope keys in a cloud KMS (AWS KMS & Google Cloud KMS) and stores customer data encrypted at rest; we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private customers (in Private deployments the customer manages keys in their VPC/HSM). We perform periodic rotation and do not re-encrypt customer ciphertexts unless explicitly requested for migration; backups are encrypted with a separate backup key. If Medita will be on Hosted, we can provide an attestation describing separation of duties and rotation cadence.

4) SOC 2 Type II (attached: redwood_socs_type2_2026.pdf) — latest report. If your procurement requires an NDA for full report disclosure, let me know and we can put one in place.

Delivery ETA: I can finalize redactions and send the secure drive link by EOD Thu (Nov 18).

Marcus
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

[attachment stubs: redwood_subprocessors_20261116.csv, sbom-inference-runtime-202611.json, kms-ownership-summary-202611.docx, redwood_socs_type2_2026.pdf]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:36:00 -08:00
Subject: Medita: requested artifacts and short answers

Hi Sarah — please find the artifacts we discussed attached and a short summary inline. If you need anything further we can jump on a call.

Summary:
- Subprocessor roster: attached CSV (redwood_subprocessors_20261116.csv). It lists providers and a "data_access" column; short-lived infra providers are grouped and flagged.
- SBOM: attached JSON (sbom-inference-runtime-202611.json) with package/version/hash. Note: build scripts and private repos are not included; hashes are deterministic and suitable for automated scanning.
- KMS / key custody: attached doc (kms-ownership-summary-202611.docx). Short answer: Hosted — Redwood manages envelope keys in AWS KMS and GCP KMS with separation of duties; Dedicated/Private — customer-managed BYOK/HSM. We do not re-encrypt customer data as part of routine backups; re-encryption only occurs during migration with customer authorization.
- SOC 2 Type II: attached PDF (redwood_socs_type2_2026.pdf). If you require a signed copy under NDA, we can provide that.

Delivery note: the attachments are in a secure Google Drive link (shared for Medita security contacts only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_shared_drive

Next steps: let us know if you need a short attestation letter for any of these artifacts or if Medita wants the subprocessor roster with individual ephemeral provider names included — we can provide a tenant-specific attestation under a non-disclosure agreement.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Vanessa — that was fast and super helpful. Quick follow-ups:

1) For the subprocessor roster, can you confirm whether ephemeral infra providers (CI runners, image-build agents) are covered under your vendor onboarding controls and SOC 2 scoping, or whether they live entirely outside SOC 2 scope? We may accept the grouped entry, but need to confirm the control coverage.

2) Also, Medita is evaluating a private deployment for HIPAA reasons. In the KMS doc you mentioned BYOK — can you send a sample key-policy and the onboarding checklist for Private deployments (what we need to provide to manage keys locally)?

If you can drop those two items by EOD Friday we can finish our intake. Otherwise let's schedule a 20 minute call.

Best,
Sarah

Medita Health
